timing: Recorded after untimed control A1 and before the first patch10 candidate observation; B1 remains queued behind E25's candidate soak.
complete: Both predeclared fixed-order eight-row comparisons must be complete and valid, with unchanged adapter and harness identities within each comparison.
primary_warming_result: Compare warm CPU milliseconds per complete cycle, not only its fraction. The mean reduction must exceed the larger within-arm range across the four timed rows. Report the fraction ratio-of-sums and per-cycle P50/P99 alongside it.
timer_intrusion: Timed A versus untimed A and timed B versus untimed B must keep selected main CPU, raw P50 and raw P99 mean shifts inside the larger within-arm range. Otherwise warming improvement remains unproven on the untimed engine.
untimed_regression: Report main, selected-process, mean-tile and total-server CPU plus every tile's raw P50/P99. Any positive regression beyond that metric's larger within-arm range prevents qualification. Changes inside spread are neutral and never CPU or tick-tail wins.
fixture_gates: Require all four untimed candidate B rows to pass the original D9 gates, with original players, routes, pigs, readers, four-core aggregate server cap and one-core bot cap. Retain every failure and never select replacements.
qualification_scope: A clear warming-time reduction with the intrusion and no-regression conditions may qualify patch10 as a warming-cost optimisation even if aggregate CPU changes remain inside noise. Do not turn neutral CPU measurements into an aggregate CPU or capacity win.
capacity: No new frontier claim. A highest step needs two passes and two fails one step above; the final combined stack still requires the reviewer's recheck.
